title: Quantifying the Quarantine
tagline: Simulating a zombie outbreak across the Czech Republic.
summary: A zombie outbreak spreading across Czechia, simulated on a 1 km population map. Every square kilometre runs Munz et al.'s humans–zombies–removed model, with zombies wandering, humans fleeing and the dead rising, as a front of bites sweeps out from Prague, Brno or Ostrava. Draw blockades and seal regions to contain it, built by a single crew at a fixed pace.
about:
**What you're seeing.** Each pixel is one square kilometre of Czechia, coloured like the chart above it. The front is where zombies are biting now, and behind it is land the zombies hold. As people are lost, the lights go out. Point at the map to read a region.

**The quarantine.** Nobody notices the outbreak until day 7. Click a region to close its borders with the rest of Czechia, or turn on *Manual blockades* under *Advanced* and draw on the map. One crew builds everything in the order you planned it, at 40 km a day, starting on the day the outbreak is detected. Nothing crosses a finished blockade, but zombies can still leave across the national border. Reset, or a new city or strain, clears the map.

**The model** is the humans–zombies–removed model of Munz et al. (2009), ["When zombies attack!"](https://loe.org/images/content/091023/Zombie%20Publication.pdf), run in every square kilometre:

- zombies bite humans, who become zombies (β); humans destroy zombies (α); and the destroyed rise again (ζ)
- zombies wander into neighbouring squares (D), and humans flee from squares where zombies are a larger share (χ)
- in a square with fewer than one zombie, zombies cannot bite, so a thin scattering of them cannot start an outbreak on its own
- zombies that cross the border are counted, and leave the model; humans stay in Czechia.

**The strains**, the detection day and the crew's speed are illustrative settings, not estimates. *Munz et al. (2009)* uses the paper's rates, reading its population of 500 as 500 people per km². *Shamblers* are slow, *Frenzied* are fast, and *Risers* lose most fights but rise again within days. Change any rate under *Advanced*.

**The summary.** The same outbreak with no quarantine runs alongside; the chart draws its humans as a dashed line. When the run ends (when the zombies are gone, or on day 365), the summary gives the survivors, and how many more that is than with no quarantine (*saved*). *Sealed in* counts the people inside each area a blockade cut off from the rest of Czechia while zombies that could bite were inside it, at the moment it closed. *Exported* counts the zombies that crossed the national border. Changes under *Advanced* apply to both runs from the same day.

**Data.** Population: [WorldPop](https://dx.doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00675), Czech Republic 2020, UN-adjusted, regridded to an equal-area 1 km grid ([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)). Boundaries: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) (public domain).
